title: scan() rejects non-UTF8 filenames; decode() accepts them
description:
scan() and decode() handle non-UTF8 bytes in the begin-line filename field differently, causing inconsistent behavior for the same input.

scan.rs parse_begin_line (line 137):
  std::str::from_utf8(filename_bytes).ok()?
This returns None on any non-UTF8 byte sequence, causing handle_block() to emit Err(InvalidBeginLine).

decode.rs (line 132):
  String::from_utf8_lossy(rest).into_owned()
This never fails; invalid UTF-8 bytes are replaced with the Unicode replacement character U+FFFD.

Result: For a begin line like 'begin 644 \xFF\xFE file.bin', decode() succeeds with a lossy filename, but scan() emits InvalidBeginLine.

Impact: Any real-world UU block with a non-ASCII (or malformed UTF-8) filename will be decoded successfully by decode() but rejected by scan() with a spurious error, breaking the documented API equivalence.

The same asymmetry applies to the mode token via std::str::from_utf8(mode_bytes).ok()? in scan.rs line 127, though non-UTF8 mode tokens are extremely unlikely in practice.

Fix: Either (a) change scan.rs parse_begin_line to use String::from_utf8_lossy for both mode and filename, matching decode.rs; or (b) change decode.rs to also use strict UTF-8 and return an error. Option (a) is preferred for real-world tolerance.
